blocks.text: PROPHET IN THE DAYS OF JEROBOAM SON OF JOASH, AND OF UZZIAH TO HEZEKIAH IN JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Hosea. Told to take “a wife of whoredoms”, he gave her children names that carried the LORD's word to Israel.
Jeroboam son of Joash · Uzziah · Jotham · Ahaz · Hezekiah
“The beginning of the word of the LORD by Hosea”
“THE BEGINNING OF THE WORD OF THE LORD BY HOSEA”
“Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD”
“The word of the LORD that came unto Hosea”. Hosea 1:1
His marriage and his children's names are part of the message. Hosea 1:2–9 Hosea 3:1–5
He speaks of the LORD's way with prophets: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes”. Hosea 12:10
The word in its main themes
“For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal”
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”
“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings”
“For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind”
“the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces”
“How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?”
“O Israel, return unto the LORD thy God; for thou hast fallen by thine iniquity”
To whom the word was spoken
“Hear the word of the LORD, ye children of Israel: for the LORD hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land”
“O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud”
“Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off”
“Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven”
2 The LORD's controversy with Israel Hosea 4:1–7:16
4 When Israel was a child Hosea 11:1–13:16
WHERE THE NEW TESTAMENT QUOTES IT · 8
Each band joins a chapter of Hosea to the New Testament books quoting it (5 books).
Who stood with him, and against him
From the textScripture tells nothing of Hosea's life after the book, or of his death. Hosea 1:1

A Jewish tradition (the Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah) says Hosea died at Babylon and that his body was carried by a camel to Safed in upper Galilee and buried there. Christian traditions make him a native of Beelmoth or Belemoth of the tribe of Issachar; Jerome, of Beth-shemesh. The Jewish Encyclopedia calls “all these stories” “historically worthless”.[19] Who says so: Later Jewish and Christian traditions (the Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah; Ephraem Syrus, pseudo-Epiphanius, Jerome), as reported in the Jewish Encyclopedia, reported 1904; the encyclopedia gives no dates for the traditions
An event in Hosea's inner vision, not an outward marriage

Keil holds that no other course is left than to picture “Hosea's marriages as internal events, i.e., as merely carried out in that inward and spiritual intuition in which the word of God was addressed to him”; yet not as “nothing more than parables” or “poetical fictions”.[9]
A real marriage to a woman already unchaste
Augustine, Ambrose, Theodoret and others, and E. B. Pusey (1860), as G. A. Smith reports (1896)
G. A. Smith reports that “a large number of other interpreters have taken the story throughout as the literal account of actual facts”, naming several Church Fathers and Pusey.[6]
A real marriage; Gomer fell later, and Hosea saw God's purpose afterwards
W. Robertson Smith (1882); G. A. Smith (1896)

G. A. Smith: “She was, therefore, no dream, this woman, but flesh and blood”. Hosea's wife was pure when he married her, and he later read back God's purpose to the day of the betrothal, because the marriage was “the beginning of the word of the LORD”. He credits the view to Robertson Smith. Hosea 1:2 [6]

Scripture does not say where Hosea lived or worked, or how he died.
Hosea 3 does not name the woman Hosea buys back; whether she is Gomer is not stated.
The “king Jareb” of Hosea 5:13 and 10:6 is not otherwise identified in Scripture.
